title: Retail Installment Contracts Servicing Standard: Posting and Applying Payments
content:
**Standard 1 — Which contracts accept payments.** On Retail Installment Contracts, a payment may be posted only to a contract whose status is active, repossessed or charged off.

**Standard 2 — Interest.** Interest is simple interest accrued daily on the principal balance at the contract's current APR on an actual/365 basis, from the later of the contract date and the date of the latest posted payment that was not returned, plus any unpaid interest carried from earlier. The accrued interest is that unpaid interest plus the principal balance multiplied by the APR percent and by the calendar days since the interest start date, divided by 365, the new interest rounded half-up to the cent. Interest is never capitalised; accrued interest a payment does not cover is carried forward as unpaid interest.

**Standard 3 — Order of application.** Every payment other than a payoff is applied in the product's order of application:

1. to accrued interest — the lesser of the payment and the accrued interest;
2. to installment principal — the lesser of what remains of the payment and the amount still needed to satisfy every installment due on or before the payment date (always at least the installment due on the next due date) less any partial installment credit already carried and less the interest portion, never below zero;
3. to fees due — the lesser of what remains and the fees due;
4. any remainder to additional principal.

The installments due are the next due date and each later due date one month apart that fall on or before the payment's posting date, never fewer than 1.

**Standard 4 — Installment credit.** The interest and installment-principal portions together are the payment's installment credit. Added to the partial installment credit, each full scheduled payment of credit satisfies one installment and advances the next due date by one month on the due day; the remainder stays as partial credit. Additional principal reduces the balance but never advances the next due date.

**Standard 5 — Payoffs.** The clause "A payment of payment type payoff must equal the payoff amount on its posting date (principal plus accrued interest plus fees due) and closes the contract" is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis for the amount of a borrower's payoff.

**Standard 6 — Recovery payments.** A reinstatement or redemption payment on a repossessed contract is applied by the same order of application, with the amounts the recovery file requires; recovery expenses are not part of the contract balance.

**Standard 7 — Fee settlement.** The fee portion of a payment settles unpaid fees in order of assessment date, oldest first; fees of the same day settle in the order late charge, returned-payment fee, agent-assisted payment fee, extension fee, reversed fee payment. It is recorded as a fee settlement linked to that payment, and the contract's principal, fees due, partial credit and next due date are refreshed after each posting.

**Worked example (hypothetical contract).** Principal 8000.00 at 20.00%, 30 days since the interest start date, no unpaid interest, scheduled payment 300.00, no partial credit, fees due 25.00, one installment due. A payment of 350.00 applies 131.51 to interest (8000.00 multiplied by 20.00% by 30 days, divided by 365), 168.49 to installment principal (300.00 less 131.51), 25.00 to fees and the remaining 25.00 to additional principal. Installment credit is 131.51 plus 168.49, that is 300.00: one installment is satisfied and the next due date moves one month.

superseded_clauses: A payment of payment_type payoff must equal the payoff amount on its posting date (principal plus accrued interest plus fees due) and closes the contract.
